3do.name: 3DO Interactive Multiplayer
3do.description: The 3DO was an ambitious multimedia console that attempted to create a standard platform for multiple manufacturers. Despite its advanced technology and CD-ROM capabilities, it failed commercially due to its high price point of $699 at launch.

3ds.name: Nintendo 3DS
3ds.description: The Nintendo 3DS is a handheld game console produced by Nintendo. It is capable of displaying stereoscopic 3D effects without the use of 3D glasses or additional accessories.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds

adam.name: Coleco Adam
adam.description: The Coleco Adam was a home computer system that could also play ColecoVision cartridges. It was designed to be an affordable all-in-one computer solution.

amiga.name: Commodore Amiga
amiga.description: The Amiga was a revolutionary computer known for its advanced graphics and sound capabilities. It became especially popular in Europe and was widely used for gaming, video production, and creative software. The Amiga pioneered multitasking and custom chipsets for graphics and audio.

amiga1200.name: Commodore Amiga
amiga1200.description: The Amiga was a revolutionary computer known for its advanced graphics and sound capabilities. It became especially popular in Europe and was widely used for gaming, video production, and creative software. The Amiga pioneered multitasking and custom chipsets for graphics and audio.

amiga500.name: Commodore Amiga
amiga500.description: The Amiga was a revolutionary computer known for its advanced graphics and sound capabilities. It became especially popular in Europe and was widely used for gaming, video production, and creative software. The Amiga pioneered multitasking and custom chipsets for graphics and audio.

amigacd32.name: Amiga CD32
amigacd32.description: The first 32-bit CD-ROM based video game console released in Western Europe. It was based on the Amiga 1200 hardware.

amstradcpc.name: Amstrad CPC
amstradcpc.description: The Amstrad CPC (Colour Personal Computer) was a popular 8-bit home computer series in Europe. It was designed to be an all-in-one computer system, with the monitor and cassette/disk drive integrated. Known for its colorful graphics and extensive game library.

apple2.name: Apple II
apple2.description: One of the first highly successful mass-produced microcomputer products. It was designed primarily by Steve Wozniak.

arcade.name: Arcade
arcade.description: Arcade games represent the commercial coin-operated entertainment machines found in public places. These machines featured dedicated hardware optimized for specific games, often more powerful than contemporary home consoles. The golden age of arcade games was from the late 1970s to mid-1990s.

atari2600.name: Atari 2600
atari2600.description: The Atari 2600 popularized cartridge-based video game consoles and is credited with bringing video games into mainstream homes. Despite the infamous video game crash of 1983, the 2600 remained popular through the mid-1980s and is one of the most iconic consoles in gaming history.

atari5200.name: Atari 5200
atari5200.description: The Atari 5200 was designed to compete with the Intellivision and ColecoVision. Based on Atari's 8-bit computer architecture, it offered superior graphics to the 2600 but suffered from reliability issues with its analog controllers and lack of backward compatibility.

atari7800.name: Atari 7800
atari7800.description: The Atari 7800 was Atari's response to the Nintendo Entertainment System. It featured backward compatibility with most Atari 2600 games and improved graphics capabilities. While technologically sound, it struggled against Nintendo's market dominance.

atari800.name: Atari 8-bit Family
atari800.description: A series of 8-bit home computers (400, 800, XL, XE) known for their advanced graphics and sound capabilities compared to contemporaries.

atarijaguar.name: Atari Jaguar
atarijaguar.description: The Atari Jaguar was marketed as the first 64-bit game console, though this claim was disputed. Despite innovative architecture with multiple processors, it suffered from a complex development environment, limited third-party support, and poor controller design. It was Atari's last console.

atarilynx.name: Atari Lynx
atarilynx.description: The Atari Lynx was the first handheld console with a color LCD screen and the first with hardware support for zooming and distortion of sprites. Despite its technical superiority, it struggled against Nintendo's Game Boy due to higher price, larger size, and shorter battery life.

atarist.name: Atari ST
atarist.description: The Atari ST was a popular home computer in Europe, known for its MIDI ports and being a rival to the Amiga.

bbcmicro.name: BBC Micro
bbcmicro.description: An educational computer very popular in the UK. Known for its rugged build and extensive expansion capabilities.

c128.name: Commodore 128
c128.description: The Commodore 128 was the successor to the Commodore 64, featuring three operating modes: C128 native mode, C64 compatibility mode, and CP/M mode via its built-in Z80 processor. It offered 128 KB of RAM, an 80-column display, and full backward compatibility with C64 software.

c64.name: Commodore 64
c64.description: The Commodore 64 is the best-selling single computer model of all time, with over 17 million units sold. It featured impressive sound and graphics capabilities for its era through the SID sound chip and VIC-II graphics chip. It dominated the home computer market in the 1980s.

cdi.name: Philips CD-i
cdi.description: The Compact Disc Interactive was a multimedia CD player developed by Philips. It is famous for several poorly received Nintendo-licensed games.

cdimono.name: Philips CD-i
cdimono.description: The Compact Disc Interactive was a multimedia CD player developed by Philips. It is famous for several poorly received Nintendo-licensed games.

cdimono1.name: Philips CD-i
cdimono1.description: The Compact Disc Interactive was a multimedia CD player developed by Philips. It is famous for several poorly received Nintendo-licensed games.

colecovision.name: ColecoVision
colecovision.description: The ColecoVision offered arcade-quality graphics and was bundled with a faithful port of Donkey Kong. It featured impressive hardware for its time and strong third-party support. The console was a commercial success until the video game crash of 1983.

cps.name: Capcom Play System
cps.description: Arcade games represent the commercial coin-operated entertainment machines found in public places. These machines featured dedicated hardware optimized for specific games, often more powerful than contemporary home consoles. The golden age of arcade games was from the late 1970s to mid-1990s.

cps1.name: Capcom Play System 1
cps1.description: Arcade games represent the commercial coin-operated entertainment machines found in public places. These machines featured dedicated hardware optimized for specific games, often more powerful than contemporary home consoles. The golden age of arcade games was from the late 1970s to mid-1990s.

cps2.name: Capcom Play System 2
cps2.description: Arcade games represent the commercial coin-operated entertainment machines found in public places. These machines featured dedicated hardware optimized for specific games, often more powerful than contemporary home consoles. The golden age of arcade games was from the late 1970s to mid-1990s.

cps3.name: Capcom Play System 3
cps3.description: Arcade games represent the commercial coin-operated entertainment machines found in public places. These machines featured dedicated hardware optimized for specific games, often more powerful than contemporary home consoles. The golden age of arcade games was from the late 1970s to mid-1990s.

doom.name: DOOM
doom.description: DOOM is a landmark first-person shooter created by id Software that revolutionized PC gaming. The PrBoom libretro core allows playing DOOM, DOOM II, and compatible WAD files. It is one of the most influential games in the history of the medium.

dos.name: MS-DOS
dos.description: Microsoft Disk Operating System was the dominant operating system for IBM PC compatibles during the 1980s and early 1990s, hosting a vast library of classic PC games.

dreamcast.name: Sega Dreamcast
dreamcast.description: The Dreamcast was Sega's final console and was ahead of its time with built-in modem for online gaming, VMU memory cards with screens, and powerful hardware. Despite critical acclaim and innovative features, it was discontinued in 2001 due to competition from PlayStation 2. It maintains a devoted fanbase today.

dsi.name: Nintendo DSi
dsi.description: An iteration of the Nintendo DS that added cameras, internal storage, and the DSiWare digital storefront.

fbneo.name: FinalBurn Neo
fbneo.description: Arcade games represent the commercial coin-operated entertainment machines found in public places. These machines featured dedicated hardware optimized for specific games, often more powerful than contemporary home consoles. The golden age of arcade games was from the late 1970s to mid-1990s.

fds.name: Famicom Disk System
fds.description: The Famicom Disk System was a peripheral for the Nintendo Famicom (Japanese NES) that used proprietary floppy disks. It offered cheaper game distribution and additional audio capabilities through an extra sound chip. It was only released in Japan.

gameandwatch.name: Game & Watch
gameandwatch.description: A series of single-game handheld LCD games produced by Nintendo. They were the first Nintendo video game products to achieve major success.

gamecube.name: Nintendo GameCube
gamecube.description: Nintendo's first console to use optical discs instead of cartridges. Known for its unique controller and compact design with a handle.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker

gamegear.name: Sega Game Gear
gamegear.description: The Game Gear was Sega's response to the Game Boy, featuring a full-color backlit screen. It had superior technical specifications but suffered from poor battery life (3-5 hours on 6 AA batteries) and higher price. It was based on Sega Master System hardware.

gb.name: Game Boy
gb.description: The Game Boy revolutionized portable gaming and became one of the best-selling consoles of all time with over 118 million units sold. Its long battery life, durability, and strong software library (especially Tetris and Pokémon) made it a cultural phenomenon despite its monochrome screen.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening

gba.name: Game Boy Advance
gba.description: The Game Boy Advance featured 32-bit processing power comparable to the Super Nintendo, bringing console-quality gaming to a portable format. It was backward compatible with Game Boy and Game Boy Color games. The GBA sold over 81 million units and had excellent battery life.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap

gbc.name: Game Boy Color
gbc.description: The Game Boy Color added color graphics to the Game Boy line while maintaining backward compatibility with original Game Boy games. It featured twice the processor speed and three times the memory of the original Game Boy, allowing for more complex games and vibrant graphics.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle series

gc.name: Nintendo GameCube
gc.description: Nintendo's first console to use optical discs instead of cartridges. Known for its unique controller and compact design with a handle.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker

genesis.name: Sega Genesis / Mega Drive
genesis.description: The Sega Genesis (Mega Drive outside North America) was Sega's most successful console, known for 'blast processing' marketing and featuring Sonic the Hedgehog as its mascot. It competed fiercely with the SNES in the early 1990s console wars and is remembered for its extensive library of action games.

intellivision.name: Intellivision
intellivision.description: The Intellivision was the first 16-bit game console and Atari 2600's main competitor in the early 1980s. It featured better graphics and a unique numeric keypad controller. Mattel marketed it as the 'intelligent television' and positioned it as more sophisticated than the Atari 2600.

jaguar.name: Atari Jaguar
jaguar.description: The Atari Jaguar was marketed as the first 64-bit game console, though this claim was disputed. Despite innovative architecture with multiple processors, it suffered from a complex development environment, limited third-party support, and poor controller design. It was Atari's last console.

lynx.name: Atari Lynx
lynx.description: The Atari Lynx was the first handheld console with a color LCD screen and the first with hardware support for zooming and distortion of sprites. Despite its technical superiority, it struggled against Nintendo's Game Boy due to higher price, larger size, and shorter battery life.

mame.name: Multiple Arcade Machine Emulator
mame.description: Arcade games represent the commercial coin-operated entertainment machines found in public places. These machines featured dedicated hardware optimized for specific games, often more powerful than contemporary home consoles. The golden age of arcade games was from the late 1970s to mid-1990s.

mastersystem.name: Sega Master System
mastersystem.description: The Master System was Sega's first cartridge-based console and competed with the NES. While technically superior to the NES with better graphics and sound, it struggled in North America due to Nintendo's dominant market position. It was more successful in Europe and Brazil.

megacd.name: Sega CD / Mega-CD
megacd.description: The Sega CD was an add-on for the Genesis/Mega Drive that added CD-ROM support, enhanced graphics capabilities, and additional sound channels. While it featured some innovative games, many releases were FMV-heavy games that aged poorly. It sold approximately 2.24 million units.

megadrive.name: Sega Genesis / Mega Drive
megadrive.description: The Sega Genesis (Mega Drive outside North America) was Sega's most successful console, known for 'blast processing' marketing and featuring Sonic the Hedgehog as its mascot. It competed fiercely with the SNES in the early 1990s console wars and is remembered for its extensive library of action games.

model2.name: Sega Model 2
model2.description: One of the most successful arcade boards ever, famous for its early 3D textured graphics.

model3.name: Sega Model 3
model3.description: A very powerful arcade board for its time, capable of rendering millions of polygons per second.

msx.name: MSX
msx.description: MSX was an attempt to create a standardized home computer architecture, promoted by Microsoft and ASCII Corporation. Multiple manufacturers produced MSX computers. It was especially popular in Japan, South Korea, Brazil, and parts of Europe. Konami developed many games for the platform.

msx1.name: MSX1
msx1.description: The first generation of the MSX home computer standard.

msx2.name: MSX2
msx2.description: The second generation of the MSX standard, with improved graphics capabilities.

n3ds.name: Nintendo 3DS
n3ds.description: The Nintendo 3DS is a handheld game console produced by Nintendo. It is capable of displaying stereoscopic 3D effects without the use of 3D glasses or additional accessories.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds

n64.name: Nintendo 64
n64.description: The Nintendo 64 was Nintendo's first 3D console, featuring 64-bit processing and an innovative analog stick controller with 4 controller ports standard. It used cartridges instead of CDs, limiting storage but eliminating load times. It introduced many 3D gaming conventions and sold 32.93 million units.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

n64dd.name: Nintendo 64DD
n64dd.description: A magnetic disk drive peripheral for the Nintendo 64. It was only released in Japan and was a commercial failure.

naomi.name: Sega NAOMI
naomi.description: The New Arcade Operation Machine Idea (NAOMI) was Sega's successor to the Model 3 and shared architecture with the Dreamcast.

nds.name: Nintendo DS
nds.description: The Nintendo DS revolutionized handheld gaming with dual screens (one touchscreen), wireless connectivity, and backward compatibility with Game Boy Advance. It became one of the best-selling game consoles ever with over 154 million units sold. The DS introduced innovative touch-based gameplay.

neogeo.name: Neo Geo
neogeo.description: The Neo Geo was a unique system that allowed users to play exact arcade versions of games at home. At $649 for the console and $200+ per game, it was marketed to wealthy enthusiasts. The Neo Geo had identical hardware for home and arcade, ensuring perfect arcade ports.

neogeocd.name: Neo Geo CD
neogeocd.description: The Neo Geo CD was a more affordable version of the Neo Geo AES, using CDs instead of expensive cartridges. Games cost around $50 instead of $200+. However, it suffered from extremely long loading times due to its 1x CD-ROM drive, which frustrated many players.

nes.name: Nintendo Entertainment System
nes.description: The NES (Famicom in Japan) revitalized the video game industry after the 1983 crash, establishing Nintendo as a dominant force in gaming. It featured the iconic controller design, strict quality control through the 'Nintendo Seal of Quality', and launched legendary franchises like Mario, Zelda, and Metroid.

ngp.name: Neo Geo Pocket
ngp.description: The Neo Geo Pocket was SNK's entry into the handheld market, featuring a clicky joystick and monochrome screen. It was quickly superseded by the Neo Geo Pocket Color. Despite quality games, it struggled against Nintendo's dominance and was discontinued in 2001.
notableGames: SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millennium

ngpc.name: Neo Geo Pocket Color
ngpc.description: The Neo Geo Pocket Color improved upon the original with a color screen while maintaining the excellent clicky joystick. It featured fighting games and puzzle games that showcased SNK's arcade heritage. Despite good reviews, it couldn't compete with Game Boy Color and was discontinued in 2001.
notableGames: SNK vs. Capcom: The Match of the Millennium

odyssey2.name: Magnavox Odyssey²
odyssey2.description: The Odyssey² (Videopac G7000 in Europe) was Magnavox's follow-up to the first home video game console. It featured a built-in keyboard and emphasized educational games alongside entertainment. While it had unique features, it struggled against the Atari 2600 and Intellivision.

pc.name: IBM PC / DOS Gaming
pc.description: IBM PC and compatible computers running MS-DOS became a major gaming platform in the late 1980s and 1990s. DOS gaming featured genres rarely seen on consoles, including complex strategy games, adventure games, and early first-person shooters. It paved the way for modern PC gaming.

pcengine.name: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16
pcengine.description: The PC Engine (TurboGrafx-16 in North America) was the first 16-bit console released and was very successful in Japan. It featured a CD-ROM add-on early in its life. Despite strong software in Japan, it struggled in North America due to poor marketing and limited game releases.

pcfx.name: PC-FX
pcfx.description: The PC-FX was NEC's successor to the PC Engine, released only in Japan. Unlike its competitors which focused on 3D graphics, the PC-FX specialized in 2D graphics and full-motion video playback. It was a commercial failure and was discontinued in 1998.

pico8.name: PICO-8
pico8.description: PICO-8 is a fantasy console designed to simulate the limitations of 1980s home computers and 8-bit consoles. It's a complete platform for making, sharing, and playing tiny games with built-in sprite, map, and music editors. The limitations (128x128 pixels, 16 colors) encourage creative game design.

pokemini.name: Pokémon Mini
pokemini.description: The smallest cartridge-based console ever made by Nintendo. It featured a monochrome screen, rumble, and a shock sensor.

ps2.name: PlayStation 2
ps2.description: The best-selling video game console of all time, with over 155 million units sold. It featured DVD playback and a massive library of games.

ps3.name: PlayStation 3
ps3.description: Sony's first console to use Blu-ray discs and high-definition output. It introduced the PlayStation Network for online gaming and multimedia services.

ps4.name: PlayStation 4
ps4.description: A powerful console focused on social gaming and connectivity. It featured the DualShock 4 controller with a touchpad and Share button.

psp.name: PlayStation Portable
psp.description: The PSP was Sony's first handheld console, featuring impressive graphics comparable to PlayStation 2, multimedia capabilities, and UMD discs. It sold over 80 million units worldwide. While it couldn't dethrone Nintendo's DS, it carved out a significant market for high-end portable gaming.
notableGames: God of War: Chains of Olympus
Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

psvita.name: PlayStation Vita
psvita.description: A powerful handheld with a high-quality OLED screen (in the original model), dual analog sticks, and a rear touchpad.

psx.name: PlayStation
psx.description: Sony's first console, the PlayStation revolutionized 3D gaming and made CD-ROMs the standard game medium. It attracted mature audiences with games like Final Fantasy VII and Metal Gear Solid. The PlayStation sold over 102 million units, making Sony a dominant force in gaming.

satellaview.name: Satellaview
satellaview.description: The Satellaview was a satellite modem peripheral for the Super Famicom in Japan. It allowed users to download games, magazines, and special content through satellite broadcasts. Notable for time-exclusive content and unique 'SoundLink' games with voice acting broadcast live.

saturn.name: Sega Saturn
saturn.description: The Sega Saturn featured powerful 2D capabilities and dual CPUs but had complex architecture that made 3D development challenging. It was very successful in Japan but struggled in Western markets against PlayStation. Known for excellent 2D fighters and shoot 'em ups.

scummvm.name: ScummVM
scummvm.description: ScummVM is a program that allows you to run classic point-and-click adventure games, primarily those using LucasArts' SCUMM engine. It supports games from multiple developers and platforms, preserving classic adventure games from the 1990s and early 2000s.

sega32x.name: Sega 32X
sega32x.description: The 32X was an add-on for the Genesis/Mega Drive meant to extend its lifespan into the 32-bit era. It was a commercial failure due to poor timing (released shortly before the Saturn), high price when combined with Sega CD, and limited software support.

segacd.name: Sega CD / Mega-CD
segacd.description: The Sega CD was an add-on for the Genesis/Mega Drive that added CD-ROM support, enhanced graphics capabilities, and additional sound channels. While it featured some innovative games, many releases were FMV-heavy games that aged poorly. It sold approximately 2.24 million units.

segastv.name: Sega Titan Video (ST-V)
segastv.description: Arcade hardware based on the Sega Saturn architecture, allowing for easy ports between the two platforms.

sg1000.name: SG-1000
sg1000.description: The SG-1000 was Sega's first cartridge-based home console, released on the same day as the Nintendo Famicom in Japan. It featured hardware similar to the ColecoVision and MSX. While overshadowed by the Famicom, it established Sega in the console market.

snes.name: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
snes.description: The SNES (Super Famicom in Japan) featured advanced graphics with Mode 7 rotation/scaling effects, excellent sound chip, and Nintendo's strongest game library ever. It competed fiercely with the Sega Genesis and sold 49.1 million units worldwide, hosting some of gaming's most acclaimed titles.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past

stv.name: Sega Titan Video (ST-V)
stv.description: Arcade hardware based on the Sega Saturn architecture, allowing for easy ports between the two platforms.

supervision.name: Watara Supervision
supervision.description: The Watara Supervision was a budget handheld console that attempted to compete with the Game Boy. It featured a larger screen but suffered from poor game quality, limited software library, and ghosting issues. It was sold under various brands in different regions.

switch.name: Nintendo Switch
switch.description: The Nintendo Switch is a hybrid console that can be used as both a home console and portable handheld. It revolutionized Nintendo's approach by unifying their handheld and home console libraries. As of 2024, it has sold over 139 million units, making it one of the best-selling consoles ever.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

vectrex.name: Vectrex
vectrex.description: The Vectrex was unique for having a built-in vector monitor, displaying crisp vector graphics instead of raster. Games came with plastic overlays for color. Despite its innovation and self-contained design, it failed due to the 1983 video game crash. It's now a sought-after collector's item.

virtualboy.name: Virtual Boy
virtualboy.description: The Virtual Boy was Nintendo's attempt at virtual reality gaming, displaying stereoscopic 3D graphics in red monochrome. It's considered one of Nintendo's biggest failures due to discomfort during use, lack of portability, limited game library, and eye strain reports. It was discontinued after less than a year.

wii.name: Nintendo Wii
wii.description: The Wii revolutionized gaming with motion controls via the Wii Remote, appealing to casual and non-gamers. It was hugely successful, selling over 101 million units and bringing gaming to wider audiences. The Wii popularized motion gaming and introduced the Virtual Console for retro games.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess

wiiu.name: Nintendo Wii U
wiiu.description: The Wii U featured a tablet-like GamePad controller with a touchscreen, allowing off-TV play and asymmetric gameplay. Despite innovative features and strong first-party games, it struggled with poor marketing, third-party support, and confusion over whether it was a new console or Wii accessory. It sold only 13.56 million units.
notableGames: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

wonderswan.name: WonderSwan
wonderswan.description: The WonderSwan was designed by Gunpei Yokoi (Game Boy creator) and was only released in Japan. It featured excellent battery life (40+ hours), could be played vertically or horizontally, and was cheaper than Game Boy. It achieved moderate success in Japan but never reached international markets.

wonderswanc.name: WonderSwan Color
wonderswanc.description: The WonderSwan Color added a color screen while maintaining backward compatibility with original WonderSwan games. It continued the excellent battery life (20+ hours with color games) and unique vertical/horizontal play. It competed well against Game Boy Color in Japan but remained Japan-exclusive.

wonderswancolor.name: WonderSwan Color
wonderswancolor.description: The WonderSwan Color added a color screen while maintaining backward compatibility with original WonderSwan games. It continued the excellent battery life (20+ hours with color games) and unique vertical/horizontal play. It competed well against Game Boy Color in Japan but remained Japan-exclusive.

wswan.name: WonderSwan
wswan.description: The WonderSwan was designed by Gunpei Yokoi (Game Boy creator) and was only released in Japan. It featured excellent battery life (40+ hours), could be played vertically or horizontally, and was cheaper than Game Boy. It achieved moderate success in Japan but never reached international markets.

wswanc.name: WonderSwan Color
wswanc.description: The WonderSwan Color added a color screen while maintaining backward compatibility with original WonderSwan games. It continued the excellent battery life (20+ hours with color games) and unique vertical/horizontal play. It competed well against Game Boy Color in Japan but remained Japan-exclusive.

x68000.name: Sharp X68000
x68000.description: The X68000 was a powerful Japanese home computer with arcade-quality graphics and sound capabilities. It was expensive but beloved by enthusiasts for its excellent arcade ports and development tools. Many Capcom arcade games were ported to X68000 first before console versions.

xbox.name: Xbox
xbox.description: Microsoft's first console brought PC-like hardware to console gaming with a built-in hard drive and Ethernet port. Xbox Live revolutionized online console gaming. Despite being a newcomer, it sold 24 million units and established Microsoft in the console market with exclusives like Halo.
notableGames: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

zx81.name: ZX81
zx81.description: The ZX81 was a popular British home computer that was one of the first mainstream home computers in the UK, sparking a generation of bedroom programmers. Despite limited color capabilities and silent keyboard, it became hugely popular due to its affordable price. It helped establish the UK games industry.

zxspectrum.name: ZX Spectrum
zxspectrum.description: The ZX Spectrum was one of the first mainstream home computers in the UK, sparking a generation of bedroom programmers. Despite limited color capabilities and silent keyboard, it became hugely popular due to its affordable price. It helped establish the UK games industry.
